newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end lower on hog crisis worries.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end lower on hog crisis worries.

text.p: Taiwan share prices ended lower on Tuesday on a continuing selloff sparked by the island's growing pork crisis and worries that it could undermine a gathering economic recovery, brokers said.

Following Monday's 287.19 point plunge, the benchmark stock index opened solidly higher on bargain hunting but was unable to hold the gains, turning lower in the final hour to finish down 103.45 points or 1.3 percent at 7,843.43. At T$124.7 billion, turnover was active but well below recent near-record highs.
A 2.31 percent rise in electronic shares helped the market find support and fend off a deeper downturn, brokers said.
"Market sentiment remained weak in the face of the export ban on pork due to the outbreak of the hog disease," said analyst Amy Huang of Nomura Securities.
She said investors were concerned that the hog crisis would jeopardise Taiwan's ongoing economic recovery
Central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said on Monday the crisis could reduce Taiwan's gross domestic product by half a percentage point in 1997.
The disease also would cost Taiwan up to US$1.55 billion in lost pork export, officials have said.
Financial, paper, and cement issues lost 2.8, 2.66 and 2.49 percent, respectively.
Taiwan Pulp and Paper fell by the daily seven-percent limit, dropping T$2.1 to close at T$27.9. Hsing Ta Cement fell T$3.1 to T$41.4.
Koahsiung Business Bank lost T$4 to T$58.5.
Brokers said concerns over a possible interest hike by the U.S. Federal Reserve pulled down the financial index.
Advanced Semiconductor Engineering Inc rose limit-up or T$5.5 to T$89 after its rating was upgraded by Lehman Brothers.
